mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that boosts equity market sentiment, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as high unemployment indicates a weakening economy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between GDP growth and housing starts drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a strong economy and housing market boost consumer spending and confidence.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals a decrease in supply chain activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate and inflation rate drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as a low interest rate and high inflation environment boosts equity market sentiment.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between GDP growth, housing starts, and consumer spending drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a strong economy, housing market, and consumer spending boost equity market sentiment.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in expansion periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 0.5% triggers a positive signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as an extremely low interest rate environment boosts equity market sentiment.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).
